cues: So could root pressure lift water up a sal tree?
It is far too small: zero point one megapascal lifts water only about ten metres.
It is strongest at night and vanishes at midday, exactly when the most water is moving.
Many conifers have none at all.
And sap still rises in stems whose living cells have been killed.
text: So could root pressure lift water up a sal tree? Four reasons say no. It is far too small: zero point one megapascal lifts water only about ten metres. It is strongest at night and vanishes at midday, exactly when the most water is moving. Many conifers have none at all. And sap still rises in stems whose living cells have been killed.
